episode_title: Should You Sell Your CPA Firm to a Non-CPA Buyer? A Buyer Explains

real_qa.q: Why did Ryan Ross build Woven software after acquiring Quality Back Office?
real_qa.r: When integrating the Quality Back Office acquisition, Ryan discovered that the software the firm needed did not exist in the marketplace. Multiple pain points emerged: QuickBooks locked his entire account for two and a half weeks holding $100,000; the payroll process with manual handwritten hours took 20-30 minutes per payroll to review; and he was paying approximately $200,000 annually across multiple disconnected platforms (QuickBooks, ADP, property management software, receipt capture). He realized all these functions should consolidate into one screen, one login, one place, which led him to build Woven with AI capabilities that can be toggled on or off.

real_qa.q: Can a non-CPA successfully acquire and run a CPA accounting firm?
real_qa.r: Yes, according to Ryan Ross, a non-CPA can successfully run a CPA practice if the business reaches a certain scale where it has stable personnel and redundancy in key roles. Ryan emphasizes that while he is not a CPA and will never be one, acquiring Quality Back Office gave him the ability to hire specialized tax managers and bookkeeping managers who provide the technical expertise. He compares it to running a hospital: 'you don't need to be a doctor to run a hospital.' The key is having really good management in place, understanding the industry deeply, knowing what clients need, and being able to scale. His successful acquisition and integration of Quality Back Office, with two more acquisitions in the pipeline, validates this approach.

real_qa.q: How should accounting firm buyers communicate a change of ownership to existing clients?
real_qa.r: Ryan Ross learned that clients want transparency about the acquisition. Clients' primary concern is whether they will still receive quality service, with their dedicated person and service level unchanged. Contrary to advice he received to 'mask' the transaction as a merger without disclosure, he chose complete honesty about what was happening. He found that masking creates problems because clients are smart and figure out the truth quickly, eroding trust. Clients tied to the previous owner required extra relationship-building and reassurance, while clients already served by other team members were easier to retain. Honesty and candidness about the transaction, including admitting mistakes when they occur, proved essential to maintaining trust in the accountant-client relationship.
real_qa.requete: How to tell clients about accounting firm acquisition

real_qa.q: What lessons from Marine Corps training did Ryan Ross apply to integrating his accounting firm acquisition?
real_qa.r: Ryan Ross, who served as a quality assurance and safety observer in the Marine Corps, brought the discipline of asking 'Why are you doing it that way?' when evaluating processes at Quality Back Office. He discovered the acquired firm had five physical offices across the country with inefficient processes, including task management software that limited communication. Rather than tearing down what the previous owner built, he applied military precision and accountability by drilling into why processes caused pain, not assuming he had all the answers, and collaborating with the seller. This approach of understanding inefficiency and systematically improving workflows, combined with his Marine Corps mindset about redundancy and delegation to reduce single points of failure, guided the post-acquisition restructuring.
real_qa.requete: Military discipline accounting firm acquisition integration

real_qa.q: What triggered Ryan Ross to shift Quality Back Office from organic growth to acquisition strategy?
real_qa.r: Ryan Ross explained that organic growth was sustainable but slow, and he recognized there were only two real paths forward: slow organic growth or acquiring firms. He also drew on his personal journey of leaving the Marine Corps to pursue accounting, where he felt called to follow a bigger vision than he initially planned. Additionally, his prior experience successfully acquiring and operating a towing company made him comfortable with the acquisition model. He and his team prayed about the decision, and when no doors closed, they pursued Quality Back Office. The acquisition strategy allowed them to supercharge their ability to serve their real estate investor client base by cross-selling tax services and significantly increasing the business multiple.

guest.bio_context: Ryan Ross left the U.S. Marine Corps in 2019 and launched TRG Bookkeeping, growing it through a hands-on advisory-first approach that treats bookkeeping as the bridge between financial performance and business results. In 2025, he transitioned from organic growth to growth by acquisition, purchasing Quality Back Office through Pro Group Advisors and rebranding it under the QBO name. During the integration of his first acquisition, he discovered existing software solutions were inadequate and built Woven, a platform consolidating general ledger, bank feeds, reconciliation, invoicing, month-end close, and client portal with AI capabilities.
